_doc: Hand-entered location codes, merged into locations.json by build_reference.py, which never writes this file. An entry here replaces a generated entry with the same key. Use the same fields as locations.json and say how each is known in `src` (game / ref / seen / user), with a `note` when it is an inference. An entry that shares a `place` with a generated one must copy that place's name, short, kind, body and system exactly (the tests check this).

INVALID_LOCATION_ID.name: No location
INVALID_LOCATION_ID.note: Printed as Location[INVALID_LOCATION_ID] in RequestLocationInventory lines when the game has no location for the player. Not a place.

stanton2.name: Crusader
stanton2.note: Planet name in terrain log lines of older builds (early 2026). Matched to the record StarMapObject.Stanton2 by name [inference].

stanton2c.name: Yela
stanton2c.note: Moon name in terrain log lines of older builds (early 2026). Matched to the record StarMapObject.Stanton2c by name [inference].

stanton4.name: microTech
stanton4.note: Planet name in terrain log lines of older builds (early 2026). Matched to the record StarMapObject.Stanton4 by name [inference].

ellis3.name: Green
ellis3.note: Planet name in terrain log lines of older builds (early 2026). Matched to the record StarMapObject.Ellis3 by name [inference]; that record's parent is the Stanton star, although the name points to the Ellis system.

patterns.name: Mission beacon
patterns.note: Quantum target made at runtime for a mission. This build has no record of this exact name, so the label is generic [inference].

patterns.name: Nav point
patterns.note: Quantum target made at runtime; the log line does not say what it marks.

patterns.name: Party Member
patterns.note: Quantum target on a party member. Label taken from the game's PARTY_MEMBER_QT_Beacon record; the link between the two names is an inference.
